programme: PPARG and NR1H2 (LXR-beta) form the classic PPAR/LXR nuclear-receptor lipid-sensing module — their target sets overlap directly on SREBF1 and LPL and both regulate cholesterol/lipid-handling genes (ABCA1, ABCG1, APOE, CETP, CD36, FABP4). ATF2, an AP-1 family bZIP factor, targets the overlapping inflammatory output of the same tissues (TNF, PTGS2, NOS2), the gene set PPARG is classically known to transrepress. Together they describe a lipid-handling/inflammatory-tone circuit rather than three unrelated hits.
role_in_a: In Ovarian_Cancer the record places PPARG directly: adipogenic reprogramming of tumor-adjacent stroma (42373903), inflammatory-cytokine genetic risk (42049359), phthalate-driven multi-omics carcinogenesis (40517225), and a Mendelian-randomization actionable-target study (42278567) — consistent with tumor cells co-opting adipocyte lipid supply. NR1H2, PPARG's obligate lipid-axis partner, has no independent ovarian-cancer citation in the record; its role here is expected by pairing, not retrieved. ATF2 has no ovarian-cancer citation at all.
role_in_b: In Stroke the same PPARG/NR1H2 pairing is directly co-studied in adipose tissue (33788111: PPARgamma, LXR-beta, RORalpha in epicardial/subcutaneous fat), with NR1H2 separately tied to macrophage-driven vascular remodeling (27021877) and PPARG to plaque stability and post-stroke pathways (40356342, 41996726, 42346122). ATF2 is independently strong here: neuronal apoptosis (42161275), mitochondrial fission in acute ischemic injury (42129133), and impaired macrophage efferocytosis destabilizing atherosclerotic plaque (39813006) — the inflammatory counterpart to PPARG/LXR-driven lipid handling in the vessel wall.
shared_axis: The same PPARG/LXR lipid-sensing circuit that lets ovarian tumors reprogram adjacent adipocytes for fatty-acid supply also governs macrophage cholesterol efflux and foam-cell/plaque biology upstream of ischemic stroke, with ATF2 providing the counter-regulated inflammatory output (TNF/PTGS2/NOS2) in both the tumor-adipocyte and vessel-wall settings. Two structurally similar lipid-rich microenvironments (omental fat versus arterial/perivascular fat and macrophages) recruit the same nuclear-receptor circuitry for different downstream ends.
reasoning: PPARG is the only factor independently documented in both diseases, and PPARG/NR1H2 are directly co-studied together in an adipose-tissue paper (33788111), so the module itself — not just each factor in isolation — has retrieved grounding rather than resting purely on reasoning. No paper states that ovarian cancer and stroke share this axis, so the pairing is 'supported' rather than 'established'; ATF2 strengthens the stroke side considerably but is entirely unretrieved for ovarian cancer, which is why the account stops short of 'established'.
support: 42373903 — adipogenic reprogramming of tumor stroma suppresses ovarian cancer progression; 42049359 — inflammatory cytokine genetic markers and ovarian cancer risk; 40517225 — phthalate-driven multi-omics ovarian carcinogenesis network; 42278567 — Mendelian randomization/experimental actionable-target study in ovarian cancer; 33788111 — PPARgamma, LXR-beta (NR1H2) and RORalpha co-expressed in epicardial/subcutaneous adipose tissue; 27021877 — hyperglycemia/macrophage suppression of aneurysm formation, NR1H2-relevant vascular macrophage biology; 40356342 — lncRNA-driven atherosclerotic plaque instability via impaired macrophage efferocytosis, PPARG-relevant; 41996726 — herbal compound mechanism improving post-stroke cognitive impairment via PPARG-linked pathway; 42346122 — PPARG deacetylation by SIRT3 in hepatic lipid regulation; 42129133 — ATF2 mRNA stability modulation driving mitochondrial fission in acute ischemic injury; 42161275 — ATF2 phosphorylation as core driver of neuron apoptosis; 39813006 — impaired macrophage efferocytosis destabilizing atherosclerotic plaque, ATF2/inflammatory-plaque relevant.
how_to_falsify: In parallel, silence NR1H2 (LXR-beta) with an antagonist or knockdown in an ovarian cancer-adipocyte co-culture/omental xenograft model and in a mouse cerebral-ischemia/atherosclerotic-plaque model. The account predicts concordant shifts in PPARG-target lipid genes (SREBF1, LPL, ABCA1) and in ATF2-target inflammatory genes (TNF, PTGS2, NOS2) in both settings. If ovarian-tumor lipid uptake or stroke plaque/neuroinflammatory phenotypes are unaffected by NR1H2 perturbation, or if PPARG and ATF2 target genes move independently of each other, the shared-axis claim fails.
caveats: The blood|ovary tissue pairing is not literally shared tissue — the lipid axis would act through different cell types (adipocytes/tumor cells in the ovarian tumor microenvironment vs. macrophages/vascular cells/microglia in blood vessels and brain), so this is a shared regulatory module, not shared cell biology. Support is drawn from 48 patient-group comparisons across only 4 independent cohort pairs; PPARG (23/48) and NR1H2 (24/48) are only moderately concordant, notably lower than THAP1 (34/48) or KAT5 (29/48), which were deliberately excluded because their target/literature profiles (dystonia-associated chromatin regulation for THAP1; Tip60/NuA4 chromatin-DNA-damage complex for KAT5) do not cohere with a lipid/inflammatory story — recurrence rank does not track mechanistic fit. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed classic blood/vascular and lymphocyte regulators (ETS1, ETS2, IKZF1, STAT5B, KLF1, SMAD3, E2F1); their absence reflects that removal, not an absence of immune signal. HSF4, GTF3A, ZFP90, TBX3, MEIS1, LHX3, ISL1 remain concordant across many groups but were left out of this account because they do not fit a lipid/inflammatory nuclear-receptor mechanism — this record should not be read as explaining all twelve listed factors.
